standard_prerequisites.use: Gives the formula I_{r_i+1}(T) = I_{r_i+1}(T_1) + I_{r_i}(T_1) that collapses the two ideals in the case j = i.

standard_prerequisites.name: Localization at primes to test an equality of ideals
standard_prerequisites.use: Reduces the general statement to the local case in which the comparison with a trivial complex can be made.

standard_prerequisites.name: The trivial two-term complex concentrated in two adjacent degrees with identity differential
standard_prerequisites.use: Is the summand Q^bullet whose addition changes I_i only by a power of f, which is exactly what the exponents m and n record.

core_obligations: Reduce the identity f^m I_i(M^bullet, f) = f^n I_i(N^bullet, f) to the case of a local ring by localizing at every prime ideal of A (proof lines 27908-27909).

Use the cited comparison lemma together with an induction argument that the author omits to replace N^bullet by M^bullet oplus Q^bullet for a trivial two-term complex Q^bullet concentrated in degrees j and j+1, with A placed there and differential the identity (proof lines 27910-27917).
Handle the case j not in {i-1, i, i+1}: the ideals and the exponents agree directly, since the extra summand is away from the relevant degrees (proof lines 27918-27920).
Handle the case j = i + 1 by observing that (f, d^i) and (f, d^i, 0) have the same nonzero minors, so again I_i agrees and m = n (proof lines 27920-27927).

Handle the case j = i by comparing r_i x r_i minors of (f, d^i) with (r_i + 1) x (r_i + 1) minors of (f oplus f, d^i oplus 1), writing the second matrix in block form T = diag(T_1, T_2) with T_2 = the column (f, 1)^t, and using I_0(T_2) = A, I_1(T_2) = A, I_p(T_2) = 0 for p >= 2 to get I_{r_i+1}(T) = I_{r_i+1}(T_1) + I_{r_i}(T_1) = I_{r_i}(T_1) (proof lines 27927-27964).
Handle the case j = i - 1, where m = n + 1, by the analogous block computation with T_2 = (f), concluding f I_i(M^bullet, f) = I_i(N^bullet, f) (proof lines 27965-27998).
difficulty_reason: The lemma fixes a nonzerodivisor f in a ring A and two bounded complexes M^bullet and N^bullet of finite free A-modules representing the same object of D(A), and asserts that f^m I_i(M^bullet, f) = f^n I_i(N^bullet, f) whenever the integers m, n satisfy a displayed Euler-characteristic condition (source lines 27892-27906). The proof localizes at every prime to reduce to comparing a complex with its sum with a trivial two-term complex (proof lines 27908-27917), and then splits into the three cases j not in {i-1, i, i+1}, j = i+1, j = i and j = i-1 (proof lines 27918-27998). The core is a minors computation: the generator sets of the two ideals are compared by exhibiting the relevant matrix in block form T with diagonal blocks T_1 and T_2 and invoking the formula for ideals generated by minors of a block matrix, which combined with I_0(T_2) = A, I_1(T_2) = A and I_p(T_2) = 0 for p >= 2 gives the required equality. This is the only candidate of the batch whose proof is a complete multi-case computation, and the author keeps the localization-and-induction reduction as an explicit step.
